text:
liam: Heads-up: we have a regression on the mixed-precision matmul path when activation quantization to FP8 is enabled. Noticed flaky outputs on long-seq evals and a 12% tail-latency spike after yesterday's runtime rollout. :bug: 

sophia: Ugh. Do you have a repro or a perf profile link? Which models/workloads are affected?

liam: repro on gpt-medium / 2k seq with KV cache warm. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/dash/abcd1234 (private). Repro script: run_eval --model gpt-medium --seq 2048 --batch 1 --quant fp8-act

anika: I pulled a quick nvprof/Tracer capture. The hot spot is in matmul kernel selection: runtime picks an FP8 fused matmul kernel for activation path but falls back to an FP16 kernel for some sequences, causing extra format conversions. Snippet from trace: 
```
[Profiler] matmul_kernel_choose: picked kernel=matmul_fp8_fused_v2
[Profiler] fallback: matmul_fp16_tile_64
[CUDA] extra memcpy & re-quantize + synchronizations
```

zach: That mismatch can create small correctness deltas + latency jitter. Might be due to the heuristic that prefers smaller tile kernels under high sequence length variance. Did the rollout change kernel thresholds?

liam: rollout had a tweak: lowered tile_threshold from 1024->768 to favor low-latency kernels for short contexts. Prob introduced a boundary case when KV cache causes effective seq len to oscillate during batching.

sophia: Can we force kernel selection to be consistent for activation quantized runs? At least until we fix heuristics. e.g., `force_kernel=matmul_fp8_fused_v2` as an option?

anika: Quick test: forcing FP8 fused kernel removes the correctness deltas in unit evals and brings tail latency down ~9%. But on some GPU/seq combos the FP8 kernel OOMs because of temporary buffers. So not a universal fix.

liam: Ok. Two-pronged plan: 1) revert the threshold tweak on the rollout to restore previous kernel-selection behavior; 2) add a safety gate: if activation quantization enabled and KV cache warm, prefer non-converting kernels or avoid mixed-kernel switching mid-request.

zach: Also we should adjust batching heuristic: when KV cache present, use effective_seq = base_seq + kv_overhead and pick kernels based on that. That'll avoid oscillation.

model-qc-bot: Run results for commit c3f9ae: quality diff report attached. Mean token-level delta: 0.0028, but a small subset of examples show token flips > 0.1 in probability. Flagging 23 failing prompts for human review.

liam: Thanks @model-qc-bot. Those 23 look like high-attention tails where small numeric change amplifies output. We'll pin them as regression-blockers.

sophia: Who's owning the rollback? I can cut a canary revert if we want to be conservative.

liam: Please do the canary revert for the runtime change to the tile_threshold. @eng-bot can you create the rollback task and schedule canary in eu-central?

eng-bot: Created task INF-4521: "Rollback tile_threshold tweak; add kernel selection safety gate". Canary scheduled to eu-central at 2026-03-18T22:15Z. Assignees: liam, anika. :white_check_mark:

anika: I'll start a patch: (a) restore threshold, (b) add condition `if activation_quant && kv_warm: prefer_consistent_kernel=true`, (c) add a metric to detect kernel switches mid-request. Patch will include unit tests that simulate KV-induced seq changes.

zach: Add a perf regression test that runs mixed-precision matmul with random seq jitter and asserts no more than 1 kernel switch per request. That should catch the oscillation in CI.

liam: Sounds good. After rollback+patch we'll re-run the long-seq evals and the QC bot. If clean, we can reintroduce threshold tweak with tuned kv-aware params.

sophia: FYI, I also saw a minor INT8 path issue on CPU fallback when FP8 kernels unavailable — outputs look quantized in the embedding layer. Separate thread?

liam: Open another thread for CPU/INT8 fallback. Let's keep this one focused on activation FP8/FP16 matmul switching. Thanks everyone. :pray:
